blocks.content: Quiz: After resolving a merge conflict in a file, what is the correct next step?
Tap an option below to answer:
Run git merge again to let Git automatically pick the winning version
Running git merge again will not resolve the conflict — Git stopped because it cannot choose automatically. You must edit the file manually, then stage and commit it.
Running git merge again will not resolve the conflict — Git stopped because it cannot choose automatically. You must edit the file manually, then stage and commit it.
Delete the branch that caused the conflict to prevent it from happening again
Conflicts are a normal part of parallel development. Deleting the branch does not fix the conflict — it removes the work. The right step is to edit, stage, and commit.
Conflicts are a normal part of parallel development. Deleting the branch does not fix the conflict — it removes the work. The right step is to edit, stage, and commit.
Stage the resolved file with git add and then run git commit to complete the merge
Correct. Once you have edited the file to remove the conflict markers and kept the right content, stage it and commit. That commit completes the merge.
Correct. Once you have edited the file to remove the conflict markers and kept the right content, stage it and commit. That commit completes the merge.
Run git restore on the file to reset it and start the merge over
git restore would throw away your resolution and put the conflict markers back. The right move after resolving is git add to stage the resolved file, then git commit.
git restore would throw away your resolution and put the conflict markers back. The right move after resolving is git add to stage the resolved file, then git commit.
